name: Honors Geometry Unit 3
description: Review parallel lines and transversals, angle theorems and converses, triangles, and equations and slopes of lines.
searchContext: honors geometry unit 3 parallel lines transversals triangles slope coordinate plane

cards.term: What makes two lines parallel?
cards.definition:
Parallel lines

Distinct coplanar lines that never intersect. Write ℓ∥k.

cards.term: Why are the highlighted edges skew?
cards.definition:
Skew lines

Their supporting lines are noncoplanar. They do not intersect and are not parallel.

cards.term: How are the top and bottom face planes related?
cards.definition:
Parallel planes

They are distinct planes with no points in common.

cards.term: What makes line t a transversal?
cards.definition:
Transversal

It intersects two or more coplanar lines at distinct points. The crossed lines can intersect each other or be parallel.

cards.term: Classify the highlighted pair ∠1,∠5 by position.
cards.definition:
Corresponding Angles

The angles occupy the same relative position at the two intersections.

cards.term: Given parallel lines, what relationship holds for ∠1,∠5?
cards.definition:
Corresponding Angles Theorem

If a transversal crosses two parallel lines, corresponding angles are congruent. Here, ∠1≅∠5.

cards.term: Given ∠1≅∠5, what can you conclude about lines ℓ and k?
cards.definition:
Converse of the Corresponding Angles Theorem

If corresponding angles formed by a transversal are congruent, then the two crossed lines are parallel. So ℓ∥k.

cards.term: Classify the highlighted pair ∠3,∠6 by position.
cards.definition:
Alternate Interior Angles

The angles lie between the lines and on opposite sides of the transversal.

cards.term: Given parallel lines, what relationship holds for ∠3,∠6?
cards.definition:
Alternate Interior Angles Theorem

If a transversal crosses two parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent. Here, ∠3≅∠6.

cards.term: Given ∠3≅∠6, what can you conclude about lines ℓ and k?
cards.definition:
Converse of the Alternate Interior Angles Theorem

If alternate interior angles formed by a transversal are congruent, then the two crossed lines are parallel. So ℓ∥k.

cards.term: Classify the highlighted pair ∠3,∠5 by position.
cards.definition:
Consecutive Interior Angles

The angles lie between the lines and on the same side of the transversal. “Consecutive” and “same-side” mean the same thing here.

cards.term: Given parallel lines, what relationship holds for ∠3,∠5?
cards.definition:
Consecutive Interior Angles Theorem

If a transversal crosses two parallel lines, consecutive interior angles are supplementary. Here, m∠3+m∠5=180°.

cards.term: Given m∠3+m∠5=180°, what can you conclude about lines ℓ and k?
cards.definition:
Converse of the Consecutive Interior Angles Postulate

If consecutive interior angles formed by a transversal are supplementary, then the two crossed lines are parallel. So ℓ∥k.

cards.term: Classify the highlighted pair ∠2,∠7 by position.
cards.definition:
Alternate Exterior Angles

The angles lie outside the lines and on opposite sides of the transversal.

cards.term: Given parallel lines, what relationship holds for ∠2,∠7?
cards.definition:
Alternate Exterior Angles Theorem

If a transversal crosses two parallel lines, alternate exterior angles are congruent. Here, ∠2≅∠7.

cards.term: Given ∠2≅∠7, what can you conclude about lines ℓ and k?
cards.definition:
Converse of the Alternate Exterior Angles Theorem

If alternate exterior angles formed by a transversal are congruent, then the two crossed lines are parallel. So ℓ∥k.

cards.term: Classify the highlighted pair ∠2,∠8 by position.
cards.definition:
Consecutive Exterior Angles

The angles lie outside the lines and on the same side of the transversal. “Consecutive” and “same-side” mean the same thing here.

cards.term: Given parallel lines, what relationship holds for ∠2,∠8?
cards.definition:
Consecutive Exterior Angles Theorem

If a transversal crosses two parallel lines, consecutive exterior angles are supplementary. Here, m∠2+m∠8=180°.

cards.term: Given m∠2+m∠8=180°, what can you conclude about lines ℓ and k?
cards.definition:
Converse of the Consecutive Exterior Angles Theorem

If consecutive exterior angles formed by a transversal are supplementary, then the two crossed lines are parallel. So ℓ∥k.

cards.term: What does it mean for two angles to be congruent?
cards.definition:
Congruent angles

∠1≅∠5 means m∠1=m∠5. The angles have equal measures.

cards.term: What does it mean for two angles to be supplementary?
cards.definition:
Supplementary angles

Their measures sum to 180°. They may be adjacent or separated.

cards.term: When two lines cross, what relationship holds for opposite angles?
cards.definition:
Vertical Angles Theorem

Vertical angles are congruent. For example, ∠1≅∠4.

cards.term: What does a linear pair tell you about the two angle measures?
cards.definition:
Linear Pair Postulate

The nonshared sides are opposite rays, so the adjacent angles are supplementary. Here, m∠1+m∠2=180°.

cards.term: How can you prove the Alternate Interior Angles Theorem for angles 3 and 6?
cards.definition:
Two-column proof reasoning

∠3≅∠2 by the Vertical Angles Theorem. ∠2≅∠6 by the Corresponding Angles Theorem. Therefore ∠3≅∠6 by transitivity.

cards.term: Given parallel lines and m∠3=68°, find m∠5.
cards.definition:
Consecutive Interior Angles Theorem

The angles are supplementary, so m∠5=180°−68°=112°.

cards.term: For what value of x are ℓ and k parallel if m∠3=(3x+10)° and m∠6=(5x−26)°?
cards.definition:
Converse of the Alternate Interior Angles Theorem

Set 3x+10=5x−26. This gives x=18, making both measures 64°.

cards.term: What makes two lines perpendicular?
cards.definition:
Perpendicular lines

They intersect to form a right angle. The square marks 90°.

cards.term: If ℓ∥k and t⟂ℓ, what follows?
cards.definition:
Perpendicular Transversal Theorem

In a plane, a transversal perpendicular to one of two parallel lines is perpendicular to the other. So t⟂k.

cards.term: If distinct coplanar lines ℓ and k are both perpendicular to t, what follows?
cards.definition:
Perpendicular Transversal Converse

ℓ∥k. Two distinct coplanar lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel.

cards.term: How many lines through P are parallel to ℓ if P is off ℓ?
cards.definition:
Parallel Postulate

Exactly one line through P is parallel to ℓ.

cards.term: What do the interior angles of any triangle add up to?
cards.definition:
Triangle Angle-Sum Theorem

m∠A+m∠B+m∠C=180°

cards.term: A triangle has m∠A=47° and m∠C=71°. Find m∠B.
cards.definition:
Use the Triangle Angle-Sum Theorem

m∠B=180°−47°−71°=62°

cards.term: How do you classify a triangle by its angles?
cards.definition:
Acute, right, obtuse, or equiangular

Acute has three angles under 90°. Right has one 90° angle. Obtuse has one angle over 90°. Equiangular has three equal angles, each 60°.

cards.term: How do you classify a triangle by its sides?
cards.definition:
Scalene, isosceles, or equilateral

Scalene has no equal side lengths. Isosceles has at least two equal side lengths. Equilateral has three equal side lengths.

cards.term: What is the sum of the two acute angles in a right triangle?
cards.definition:
The acute angles are complementary

180°−90°=90°. The right angle uses half of the triangle’s total angle measure.

cards.term: In the diagram, why is ∠CBD an exterior angle?
cards.definition:
Exterior angle of a polygon

It is formed by a side and the extension of an adjacent side. Ray BD extends side AB beyond B.

cards.term: Which interior angles are remote to exterior angle CBD?
cards.definition:
Remote interior angles

The two interior angles away from the exterior angle’s vertex are ∠A and ∠C.

cards.term: How does the measure of exterior angle CBD relate to the two remote interior angles?
cards.definition:
Triangle Exterior Angle Theorem

An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angle measures. m∠CBD=m∠A+m∠C.

cards.term: If m∠A=38° and m∠C=61°, find m∠CBD.
cards.definition:
Use the Triangle Exterior Angle Theorem

m∠CBD=38°+61°=99°.

cards.term: How do you find the slope between two points?
cards.definition:
Slope is rise divided by run

Divide the change in y by the change in x. A vertical line has undefined slope.

m=y2−y1x2−x1

cards.term: The line rises 2 units over a run of 3 units. What is its slope?
cards.definition:
Rise over run

m=23

cards.term: Reading left to right, how can you recognize the four slope types?
cards.definition:
Positive, negative, zero, and undefined

Positive rises. Negative falls. Horizontal has zero slope. Vertical has undefined slope.

cards.term: What is slope-intercept form, and what do m and b tell you?
cards.definition:
Slope-intercept form

y=mx+b. The slope is m and the graph crosses the y-axis at (0,b).

cards.term: What form is quickest when you know a point and a slope?
cards.definition:
Point-slope form

Use m for slope and substitute the coordinates of one point.

y−y1=m(x−x1)

cards.term: What are the equations of the horizontal and vertical lines through (2, 4)?
cards.definition:
Horizontal and vertical equations

Horizontal: y=4. Vertical: x=2. Each equation fixes one coordinate.

cards.term: When do two distinct nonvertical lines have parallel graphs?
cards.definition:
Slopes of Parallel Lines

Exactly when their slopes are equal, m1=m2 Two distinct vertical lines are also parallel.

cards.term: How can slopes show that two nonvertical lines are perpendicular?
cards.definition:
Slopes of Perpendicular Lines

Their slopes are negative reciprocals, so their product is −1. A horizontal line and a vertical line are also perpendicular.

m1·m2=−1

cards.term: Write the equation of the line parallel to y=−3x−5 that passes through (−1,8).
cards.definition:
Keep the same slope

y−8=−3(x+1), so y=−3x+5.

cards.term: Write the equation of the line perpendicular to y=−3x−5 through (−3,7).
cards.definition:
Use the negative reciprocal

The perpendicular slope is 13 Point-slope form gives y−7=13(x+3)

cards.term: Line 1 goes through (2, 7) and (3, −1). Line 2 goes through (−2, 6) and (8, 7). Are they perpendicular?
cards.definition:
Check the slope product

Line 1 has slope −8. Line 2 has slope 110 Their product is −45 No. The lines would need a slope product of −1 to be perpendicular.
